text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people.** NMC only makes sense in a few cases, described below.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** This is the biggest gap. The same-maker pairs in OutageMath's data show it clearly. Goal Zero's NMC Yeti 1500X is rated 500 cycles to 80%, and its LFP Yeti 1500 is rated 4,000 to 80%. At one full cycle a day, 500 cycles lasts about 1.4 years and 3,000 lasts about 8 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells failed more mildly. They peaked at lower temperatures and, in one test, gave off smoke without flames, while the NMC cells ignited. LFP is not fireproof, though. In one overcharge test it reached thermal runaway sooner ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Some retail-style sites claim LFP is "virtually impossible" to ignite, which overstates the research.
- **Price:** One retailer guide puts the median at about $0.55 per Wh for LFP versus $0.95 for NMC, and LFP is cheaper per rated cycle ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Nearly every mid-size and large current model is LFP.

**Where NMC wins**
- NMC cells hold more energy per kilogram. In finished stations the gap shrinks a lot, because the case, inverter and fans weigh the same either way. OutageMath found only about 10% more Wh per pound for the median NMC unit. Some LFP stations are even lighter per Wh than some NMC ones, so compare specific models.

**Caveats**
- **Cold weather:** Sources disagree on whether LFP handles cold better. Several manuals show both chemistries refusing to charge below 32°F, and the limits depend more on the maker than the chemistry. Check the manual of the unit you buy.
- **Cycle ratings:** Makers don't all rate to the same endpoint (70% vs 80%), and test conditions differ. Compare ratings carefully.
- **Light use:** If you'll cycle it only a few times a year, such as for rare outages, cycle life matters much less. Calendar aging and storage become the limit. You can choose on weight and price.

**Decision guide**
- **Daily or frequent use** (van, cabin, solar, UPS): LiFePO4.
- **Home backup:** LiFePO4.
- **Weight-critical or occasional use:** either one, but check the specific model.
- **You already own a working NMC unit:** keep using it.
